item.title: News Wrap: Xi wraps up 3-day state visit with Trump
item.description:
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping have barely finished shaking hands in Washington, and they already have two more face-to-face meetings on the calendar. Xi announced Friday that he and Trump will meet again in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit November 18-19 in Shenzhen, China, and then again in December at the G20 summit at Trump National Doral in Miami. If both meetings take place as planned, Trump and Xi will have met face-to-face four times in 2026 — an “unprecedented” frequency for the leaders of the world’s two largest economies, according to Wu Xinbo, director of the Center for American Studies at Fudan University. The meetings will mark a remarkable burst of personal diplomacy between Washington and Beijing. Trump and Xi first met this year in May, when Trump traveled to Beijing. item.title: Pope Leo XIV warns AI could undermine humanity during France visit
item.description:

item.title: Manchester City reportedly found guilty of almost 115 financial charges
item.description:
The Premier League has reportedly given Manchester City a major red card. City has been found guilty of more than 100 financial charges that were brought by the league over an eight-year period, according to a report from The Athletic. The punishment has not been decided, and City is expected to appeal potential sanctions, according to the report. "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023," City told The Athletic in a statement. item.title: Xi wraps up US visit with trip to National Archives
item.description:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping departed Washington this afternoon after a three-day trip that led to no significant breakthroughs on the two country’s disagreements, including on AI, Taiwan and Iran. Xi broached Taiwan to Trump, per a readout from Beijing, and Trump asked Xi to stop supporting Iran , US Ambassador to Beijing David Perdue said . Officials also discussed extending their trade truce until January and staying in touch about AI, Treasury Department Scott Bessent said earlier this week. But there were no major announcements with the countries still at odds on most fronts, including its growing nuclear arsenal. That could change later this year, when Xi said he would see Trump at the APEC summit in China and the G20 summit in the US. Xi also invited Trump back to China in the spring. item.title: Which countries walked out of Netanyahu’s UNGA speech?
item.description:
More than 100 people were arrested at large protests against the Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the UN general assembly. Susan Sarandon, Chelsea Manning and Caleb Hearon were among the famous faces arrested. Inside the assembly hall, Netanyahu faced a mass walkout as he took to the stage. Then, in an inflammatory address, he claimed Israel’s war in Gaza was the ‘opposite of a genocide’ and labelled the New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, antisemitic. item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping landed at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington on Wednesday and was met personally on the tarmac by President Donald Trump. The agenda included an elaborate Rose Garden military review and official state dinner in the White House's East Room. item.title: Macron says ‘military resources’ to be sent to Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, pushing oil prices up on fears the Middle East conflict could expand and intensify. Though Riyadh recently signed a mutual defense agreement with Pakistan and Türkiye, neither has been willing to deploy troops to help the kingdom, forcing Saudi Arabia to turn to European countries for assistance. The Trump administration has also failed to come to Saudi Arabia’s aid despite their long-term defense relations, a decision that risks further fraying ties between the erstwhile allies. Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler “ will not forget this ,” a former senior US defense official told the Financial Times. — Jeronimo Gonzalez
